name: The Last Survey
status: Working direction — references are provisional, not approved final art
intent: Claustrophobic subterranean horror. Darkness carries the composition; a warm handheld beam reveals damp cool limestone and an almost human silhouette.
shapeLanguage: Layered limestone walls, rounded eroded passages and sharp mineral fractures. The Watcher has long asymmetric limbs and a narrow bone mask.
detailBudget: Express identity in silhouette and broad color masses first. Surface detail supports form at normal play distance; avoid photographic microdetail on one asset beside simplified neighbors.
materials: Rough limestone, damp seams, a worn metal beacon, matte charcoal skin and a chalky mask. Avoid bright ambient fill.
color: Desaturated gray-green rock, ivory mask, a warm beam, one cyan beacon accent.
reviewQuestions: Do these objects share a level of simplification and a readable shape language?
Does detail density remain consistent at comparable viewing distances?
Do roughness, saturation and contrast belong to the same painted world?
Does each material remain recognizable under both lights without exposure compensation?
What is the deliberate focal point, and what detail can be removed?
lighting: One atmosphere and lighting model across the world. Preserve warm/cool separation and readable shadow values; avoid unrelated exposure fixes per object. Clouds need broad, readable masses with controlled small detail and coherent light direction.
